media_work.title: 3 ½ Minutes, 10 Bullets
media_work.focus_or_theme: Examines the 2012 shooting death of 17-year-old Jordan Davis by Michael Dunn, exploring the trial, "Stand Your Ground" law, and racial bias.
media_work.summaryNotes: Dunn fired 10 bullets into the car occupied by Davis and three friends. Dunn was convicted of first-degree murder in a retrial.

media_item.focus_or_theme: Examines the 2012 shooting death of 17-year-old Jordan Davis by Michael Dunn, exploring the trial, "Stand Your Ground" law, and racial bias.
media_item.summary_notes: Documentary examining the shooting death of Jordan Davis and the subsequent trial of Michael Dunn, highlighting issues of self-defense laws and racial bias.
key_quotes_raw: Courtroom footage from Michael Dunn's trials
Analysis of the "Stand Your Ground" law
Recordings of Dunn's phone calls from jail
systemic_issues_raw: Controversial self-defense laws ("Stand Your Ground") and their application
Potential for racial bias in perceptions of threat and in the justice system
Disparate outcomes in interracial violence cases
The impact of gun violence on families and communities
policy_recommendations_raw: Implicitly calls for re-examination and reform of "Stand Your Ground" laws
Addressing racial bias within the justice system

external_links_raw.description: Information from Everytown for Gun Safety, news archives covering the Jordan Davis case and Michael Dunn trials.
